text:
ken: FYI, around 02:12-02:30 UTC in euw1-dedicated-pool-3 we hit a near-OOM sequence during a retail promo. No 5xxs but throttling->95% for ~6m while autoscaler lagged.
raj: saw metric spike on dashboard. GPU mem rose sharply while pod CPU stayed low; looks like huge prefix/KV cache growth from many long-lived streaming sessions.
anya: can you paste a concise timeline and which model variants were receiving traffic?
ken: timeline:
02:10 traffic uptick begins (campaign surge)
02:14 transient packet loss ~30s (network jitter)
02:15 kvcache growth accelerates
02:17 GPU mem ~93% and kube evicted 2 pods (OOM mitigation)
02:18 routing fallback to smaller model variant
02:21 autoscaler kicked and added pods
02:27 latency back to baseline
hot models: rdx-llama-70b-quant (main), rdx-gnmt-7b (fallback)
maria: no customer-facing errors reported. Dedicated tenants saw higher latency; operational headroom consumed which will affect cost reporting for the day.
raj: logs excerpt:
```
2026-04-03T02:16:49Z gpu0 mem_used=93.7% kvcache_entries=1_200_345 prefix_hit_rate=0.12
2026-04-03T02:16:52Z pod/generator-23 OOM_score_adj triggered
```
anya: 1.2M kvcache entries is beyond our safe threshold. Combined with the small network blip that kept streams open, session histories ballooned.
ken: root-cause hypothesis: (A) unexpected long-stream pattern from the campaign, (B) autoscaler only looks at CPU + token throughput and thus reacted too late to memory pressure.
maria: what are options to balance cost vs reliability? can we quantify incremental cost of earlier scaling vs risk of throttles?
ken: rough estimate: each extra pod costs ~1.2 GPU-hours per pod-hour. We added ~4 pods, but timing means ~0.4 GPU-hours extra during the 6m window. Not huge for single event, but frequent recurrence matters.
raj: suggested mitigations:
- extend autoscaler signals to include gpu_memory and kvcache_entries
- add alert for sustained kvcache growth (e.g., >900k for 2m)
- policy to cap per-session history length or apply aggressive eviction for Dedicated during promos
- create a warm-burst prewarmed pool to absorb campaign spikes
- low-latency smaller-model pool prewarmed to avoid latency hit on fallback
anya: will prototype kvcache-aware scaling rule in staging. also schedule TTL/ejection tests for session history (30s eviction experiment).
lee: finance: I'll compute monthly cost delta of keeping 10% additional headroom for euw1 and share Wednesday.
maria: action owners:
- eng-runtime (raj): PR to add kvcache_entries/gpu_mem to HPA by EOD Friday
- infra (anya): warm-burst pool template + rollout guide
- product (maria): campaign checklist and session-length guidance for customers
- finance (lee): headroom cost estimate
ken: doc incident in postmortems with tags: capacity/kvcache/autoscale/network. We’ll review at Ops Sync Monday.
infra-bot: [02:35] INCIDENT INC-2026-234 auto-tagged post-analysis
maria: noted. I’ll coordinate a short customer-facing note if any tenants want reassurance. Closing the thread for now :thumbsup:
